_meta.experiment: E2 directionality (minimal-edit counterfactuals, scored on action-consequences)

scoring.scored_span: the answer_next_action tokens only (the NEXT-STEP action/code the matched direction implies); NOT 'what happened first' recall
scoring.discriminator: control_lp - counterfactual_lp > 0 (the control absorbs lexical/position overlap so the residual is the causal flip); matched - counterfactual is reported too but is the weaker, lexically-confounded contrast
scoring.ceiling_fraction: (matched_lp - zero_lp) reported as a fraction of (ceiling_lp - zero_lp), per spec E2 ceiling arm

_meta.harness: third_party/doc-to-lora/rune_episode_recall.py — matched=own doc (ctxs[i]); counterfactual REPLACES the (i+1) structured-negative ctx at line 94; control is a sibling ctx for the additional matched-vs-control contrast; zero=base; ceiling=doc-in-prompt no-adapter (already present).
_meta.doc_format: ## Task / ## Current Code / ## Review Feedback headers, adapted in STRUCTURE from real external_codereview rows (/tmp/rune-corpus/external_codereview.val.clean.jsonl) and tools/d2l_control/episodes.py::_SYNTHETIC_ROWS. All episodes are SYNTHETIC content (the provable direction-flips-action property requires authored content); they mimic the real doc shape.
_meta.forbidden_avoided: NO bare time-reversal; NO were<->heading lexical swaps. Flips live in STATE/ROLE semantics (what currently exists vs is missing; which function is the caller vs callee; which layer depends on which), distributed across the doc so there is no single sentinel token a model can exploit without modeling direction. counterfactual_doc and control_doc are constructed to be ~equidistant lexically from matched_doc.
_meta.construction_rule: Per episode: matched_doc states the true causal state; counterfactual_doc minimally edits ONLY the causal arrow (state/role swap), preserving tokens/local code; control_doc has the SAME bag of events as matched_doc but neutrally reordered (no directional flip), so the correct next action is UNCHANGED. answer_next_action is the next edit implied by matched; under the counterfactual it is WRONG (a different edit is correct, documented in counterfactual_next_action).
_meta.validity_invariant: For every episode: under the flipped (counterfactual) direction the scored answer_next_action is NOT the correct next edit. Episodes where the flip leaves the correct next action unchanged are excluded by construction.
_meta.priming_invariant: The adapter ENCODES facts stated in its conditioning doc and RAISES their logprob (cf. the project's +2.235 goal recall). Therefore the scored answer's distinguishing body tokens must NOT be stated by the counterfactual_doc more than by the matched_doc; otherwise the flipped adapter would LIFT the scored span and invert control_lp - counterfactual_lp. tools/_e2_build.py::check_episode enforces this structurally (the GPU run confirms it in logprobs). An earlier lock-ordering episode was DROPPED because its corrected end-state was identical under both directions (tested recall, not direction); replaced by cf_cache_source_of_truth.
_meta.expected_warnings: pc_test_vs_code carries an INTENTIONAL lexical-imbalance WARN: a positive-control state-flip rewrites the whole state description, so the counterfactual diverges more lexically than the no-flip control. The PC's headline is matched/ceiling >> counterfactual (a large gap is the goal); do not weaken the flip to balance lexical distance.
_meta.dropped_episodes: A caller/callee RENAME episode (compute_total -> compute_grand_total) was DROPPED. A rename's scored answer IS a specific identifier that must be stated somewhere, so it cannot be 'inferred from state, absent from both docs' the way the action/API episodes are. Any framing either (a) primes the scored token in the counterfactual (current-state leak), or (b) uses a different identifier in the counterfactual, which makes control vs counterfactual differ in the NAME as well as the direction -> the control_lp - counterfactual_lp discriminator then measures name-recall, not direction (the FORBIDDEN lexical artifact). Rename episodes are a structural mis-fit for E2's lexicon-controlled design; excluded. The 5 kept episodes all have control and counterfactual sharing their full lexicon (same files, same API surface), differing only in WHICH SIDE LEADS, with the answer code inferred from state.
_meta.harness_gap: rune_episode_recall.py scores matched(ctxs[i]), counterfactual(ctxs[(i+1)%len]), zero, ceiling. There is NO scoring slot for control_doc. The headline discriminator control_lp - counterfactual_lp is therefore UNCOMPUTABLE until a third conditioning pass for control_doc is added to the harness (one extra logits_with_ctx call + a per_target['*_ctrl'] column). This loader emits control_doc ready to drop in; the harness wiring is a required GPU-side add.
